title: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality
read_level: full (main contribution skimmed; WSP appendix I read in full)
why_wsp: Main paper is RL plus VR human demonstrations for grasping; one exploratory appendix has Claude Opus 5.5 read and edit the 2.2M-parameter Contact-GraspNet teacher via IWIBench tensor tools without gradients, testing candidates on practice objects.
target: Contact-GraspNet grasp generator, 'the network’s 2.2M parameters' (Appendix I)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (candidates measured on practice objects, then reverted)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: two bias edits tried (a normalization bias in the head; output bias raised 'to 1.623'); both reverted. Exact count not stated.

headline_results.claim: Editor found a structural score ceiling in the released checkpoint
headline_results.quote: no grasp can score above σ(−0.877) = 0.294, and a grasp reaches this value only when all 128 inputs are zero (1.3% of points)

headline_results.claim: Both edits lowered practice success and were reverted (negative result)
headline_results.quote: Both edits lowered practice success (flat 85 to 79 and 83; tilted 55 to 53 and 51), so the model reverted them and submitted the unedited weights.
Adding 58 human demonstrations nearly doubles success on the hard cases RL kept failing, from 24% to 45%

baselines_and_controls: unedited Contact-GraspNet on practice objects (116 flat and 116 tilted episodes); test families and seeds withheld from editor
runs_and_variance: WSP part: single run. Baseline variance noted: regenerating labels with a different camera viewpoint 'gave 64.0% flat and 39.5% tilted on 200 episodes each ... against 55.1% and 50.3% in Table II' (Appendix I)
memorization_vs_reasoning: Editor identified a mechanistic property (all-negative final weights after ReLU cap confidence), confirmed on ~475k points; authors frame edits as 'modulatory' in IWIBench terms.
limitations_stated: For WSP appendix: practice-set group comparison 'is not causal'; result negative. Main paper limitations concern case selection bias against RL-alone.
notes_for_survey: WSP appears only as an exploratory negative result: the LLM editor correctly diagnosed a confidence ceiling in Contact-GraspNet but removing it did not improve grasp success, so the edits were reverted. Useful as an example of a read-then-repair attempt where the diagnosed obstacle was not the performance bottleneck.
